title: 2-D Shapes
tagline: Sides, vertices and lines of symmetry
dadNotes: Count each side once and only once: put a finger on the first side you counted.
Say it the school way: 'This shape is a hexagon because it has exactly 6 straight sides.'
Year 2 only needs a vertical line of symmetry: a fold straight down the middle.

lines: Look at these 3 space station windows.
steps.question: What is the same about them?

steps.text: Have you counted sides and vertices at school?

steps.prompt: How many sides does this star have?

then: This shape is a pentagon because it has exactly 5 straight sides.
hint: Start at the top and go round one way.
Each side you tap turns blue with a number.

say: A vertex is where 2 sides meet.
then: The same as the number of sides!
hint: A vertex is a pointy corner.

then: 6 straight sides, so it is a hexagon.
A hexagon does not have to look neat.
hint: Go round one way, like a clock hand.

say: Tap every vertex on this one.
hint: Do not miss the corner that points inwards.
It counts as a vertex too.

say: How many sides does an octagon have?
Tap to count, then type it.
then: 8 sides. Octo means 8, like an octopus.
hint: Tap each side. The blue numbers count for you.

say: The dashed line goes down the middle.
then: The dashed line is a line of symmetry.
hint: Watch the left half flip over.

then: It has no vertical line of symmetry.
hint: Does the left half land on the right half?

then: They match. A vertical line of symmetry!
hint: Watch where the left half lands.

say: Does this one have a vertical line of symmetry?
Decide first, then fold to check.
then: No. The two halves are different.
hint: Imagine folding it along the dashed line.
Would the halves match? Tap Fold to check.

intro: Your turn. Count each side once.

steps.title: Which one doesn't belong?
reveal: Circle: the only one with a curved side.
Triangle: the only one with 3 sides.
Rectangle: the only one with long and short sides.
Square: the only one with 4 sides all the same length.
steps.followUp: Every one can be the odd one out! Can you find another reason?

intro: {engineer} counted the sides of a hexagon.
lines: Counting the sides of a hexagon
Side 7: back at the first side!
fix: The first side was counted twice.
Count each side once and only once: 6 sides.

steps.title: Fold and cut
steps: Fold a sheet of paper in half.
Cut a shape along the fold.
Open it up. What do you notice?
steps.why: The fold is a line of symmetry, so both halves match.

debrief: How can you check if a shape has a line of symmetry?

warmup.say: First, a quick warm-up: name some shapes.
